title: The Materials Lab
summary: Find H, M and B in a core, classify materials by susceptibility, and apply Curie’s law.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find H, M and B in a filled solenoid, relate susceptibility and permeability, classify materials, and say how paramagnetic susceptibility changes with temperature.

levels.title: A filled solenoid
levels.adds: Baseline: H = nI, M = χH, and B = μ₀(H + M) = μ₀μᵣH (Section 5.4).
hints: H depends only on the turns per metre and the current.

levels.title: Which kind?
levels.adds: New idea: μᵣ = 1 + χ, and the sign and size of χ tell the kind of material (Table 5.2).
hints: A small negative χ is diamagnetic, a small positive χ paramagnetic.
A large positive χ is ferromagnetic.

levels.title: Hot and cold
levels.adds: New idea: for a paramagnet χ is proportional to 1/T, as thermal motion fights the alignment (Section 5.5.2).
hints: Cooling raises χ; heating lowers it.
Use the ratio of the temperatures in kelvin.

levels.title: Near a magnet
levels.adds: Apply it: diamagnetic samples are repelled, paramagnetic ones weakly attracted and ferromagnetic ones strongly attracted (Section 5.5).
hints: Diamagnetic materials move from strong to weak field.
Paramagnetic atoms have permanent moments that only partly line up.

misconceptions: Only iron is affected by a magnet
The susceptibility of a paramagnet does not depend on temperature
A diamagnetic material is attracted to a magnet
H and B are the same thing
